title: pkix-chain: async verify path (requires an async Verifier, not a wrapper)
description:
## Why

PKIX-j32w.3 decided pkix-chain would grow an async twin of its DANE-relevant verify entry points, and recorded that the async path must be async ALL THE WAY DOWN: an entry point that awaited TLSA resolution and then called a synchronous RevocationChecker or AiaFetcher would block the executor on that I/O, which is the defect already open against pkix-revocation-http as PKIX-cr8.1 and PKIX-f1j4.10.

The sync DANE composition shipped in pkix-chain 0.6.0. The async twin did not, because implementing it revealed the scope is materially larger than "add async siblings to a few functions".

## The actual scope

verify_tls_server does not perform validation itself. It calls verify_chain, which constructs a Verifier and calls verify_one, which calls:

- build_with_aia -- roughly 99 lines, and itself calls try_build
- run_revocation_checks -- roughly 18 lines

Both touch the I/O traits. So an async verify_tls_server_dane needs an async Verifier with async counterparts of verify_one, build_with_aia, try_build and run_revocation_checks, generic over AsyncRevocationChecker and AsyncAiaFetcher instead of their sync forms. That is duplicating pkix-chain's orchestration layer, not wrapping it.

Everything it depends on now exists: AsyncTlsaResolver (pkix-dane-resolver 0.2.0), AsyncRevocationChecker (pkix-revocation-http, behind its async feature), AsyncAiaFetcher (pkix-aia-http 0.3.0, PKIX-j72x). The missing piece is entirely inside pkix-chain.

## Decide before building

1. Duplicate or unify. A parallel AsyncVerifier is straightforward and matches how pkix-revocation-http handled the same problem, but it doubles the orchestration surface -- and build_with_aia is where the AIA bounds from PKIX-zkjb.7 live, so the two copies drifting is a correctness risk, not just a maintenance one. The alternative is making the orchestration generic over a sync-or-async I/O abstraction, which is more invasive and may not be worth it. Decide explicitly rather than defaulting to duplication because it is easier to start.

2. Scope of the async surface. PKIX-j32w.3 recorded that only DANE-relevant entry points need async siblings, and that adding the rest on symmetry grounds buys nothing. That still holds, but verify_one and verify_batch are generic entry points consumers use directly, so decide whether they get async forms too.

3. SignatureVerifier stays sync -- signature verification is CPU-bound, nothing to await. Note that PKIX-cr8.1 and PKIX-f1j4.10 argue ms-scale CPU inside an async fn is itself a problem deserving spawn_blocking. That question is broader than DANE and should not be settled here, but it will come up.

## Acceptance

[ ] Duplicate-or-unify decision recorded before code is written
[ ] An async DANE entry point exists that awaits TLSA resolution, revocation AND AIA -- no sync I/O trait on the async path
[ ] AIA bounds (per-cert URI cap, total fetch cap, deadline) behave identically on both paths, with tests that would fail if the two copies drifted
[ ] The sync path is unchanged
